sections.voiceover: In 1897, Bram Stoker designed his castle using Romanian landscape references. Journals from Jonathan Harker near Bistritz relied on the language of war. Why did an Ordnance Map fail to locate the castle?
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom into vintage 1897 map of Transylvania near Bistritz, switching to handwritten journal pages with tactical defense notes.
sections.sfx_cue: Quill scraping parchment, subtle low ambient tone
b_roll: 19th century map of Transylvania Bistritz region

sections.voiceover: However, researcher Alexander found Harker's journals used war language without locating Castle Dracula near Bistritz.
sections.visual_cue: Cross-section architectural diagram highlighting defensive stone walls, secret passages, and hidden entryways.

sections.voiceover: Architectural studies by Sukdolová documented secret passages, round arches, and tall black windows. That sheer drop measures 1000 feet straight down.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic camera movement through vaulted stone arches, tall black pointed windows, and over hanging battlements projecting against the sky.
sections.sfx_cue: Echoing footsteps in stone hall, thunder rumble
b_roll: Tall pointed arched windows skyline silhouette

sections.voiceover: Drop a stone from the window to watch it fall 1000 feet without touching anything.
sections.visual_cue: Wide dramatic shot of Castle Dracula silhouette perched atop an isolated mountain pinnacle.
sections.sfx_cue: Final subtle wind gust fade out
